value.body: Works with maps and location data — digitising features, processing satellite or drone images, and running spatial analysis. Mapping and survey firms, infrastructure and utility companies, environmental consultancies and government projects hire GIS analysts. Most of the day is at a computer working in GIS software.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Sc / M.Sc in Geology, Geography or Environmental Science, or a B.Tech
items.note: A GIS / remote-sensing certificate or PG diploma helps

items.label: Common tools
items.value: QGIS, ArcGIS, GPS data, satellite imagery, spreadsheets

items.note: A 2022 projection (~12.8% annual growth), not a measured figure

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers often start as GIS technicians or executives in mapping and data-processing firms, doing digitisation work, then move to analysis. A short course in GIS and remote sensing, plus a small portfolio of maps, is what interviews usually look for.

value.title: At a glance
items: Entry digitisation work can be repetitive; analysis roles come with experience.
Growth path: GIS technician → analyst → GIS specialist or project lead.
Programming skills open geospatial data and developer roles.
